phone.why: The best-scoring open model this small that also reads pictures, so one download covers a phone.

laptop.why: The highest independent score among open models that fit 16 GB.

workstation.why: The highest independent score among open models from 4B to 40B.

server.why: No larger openly licensed model scores higher; this is the same model at full precision.

phone.why: Reads a 262K-token window; a phone's memory keeps the usable part far smaller.

laptop.why: Recalls more over long inputs than Gemma 4 12B on an independent long-reading test.

workstation.why: Recalls about 82 percent over long inputs, ahead of the 1M-token models that fit here.

server.why: Full precision with room for the whole 262K window.

laptop.why: Scores 64.4 on MedQA against 50.7 for its general base, and reads CT, MRI and X-ray images (Google's numbers).

workstation.why: Scores 87.7 on MedQA against 74.9 for its general base (Google's numbers).

phone.why: Scores 77.1 on GPQA Diamond (the publisher's number), well ahead of other models this size.

laptop.why: Leads its size on an independent reasoning index.

workstation.why: Scores 89.2 on GPQA Diamond (the publisher's number).

server.why: The same model at full precision.

phone.why: Scores 79.9 on tau2-bench, a test of using tools to finish a task.

laptop.why: Scores 66.1 on BFCL v4 and 79.1 on tau2-bench.

workstation.why: Scores 73.0 on Terminal-Bench 2.1.

server.why: The same model at full precision.

laptop.why: Scores 72.0 on LiveCodeBench v6, ahead of Qwen3.5 9B.

workstation.why: Scores 61.7 on SWE-bench Pro, ahead of every other open model that fits here.

server.why: The same model at full precision.

laptop.why: No writing score exists at this size yet; it leads its size on an independent index, and its larger sibling matches far bigger models on a creative writing test.

workstation.why: Matches models many times its size on a creative writing benchmark (a third-party snapshot), and runs fast.

laptop.why: Trained on more than 140 languages, and it chats, so it fills the Writing slot.

workstation.why: The larger Gemma 4, with the same 140-plus languages.

phone.why: Scores 74.0 on the February 2025 HMMT problems.

laptop.why: Scores 83.2 on the same problems, ahead of gpt-oss-20b.

workstation.why: Scores about 99 on AIME 2026 in an independent run.

server.why: The same model at full precision.

laptop.why: Scores 76.5 on ChemBench against 61.1 for Qwen3 8B (the publisher's numbers).
The top open embedder under 1B on code and multilingual search, and quick on a CPU.

workstation.why: The top score in its family on code and multilingual search.

phone.why: Rated the leading open model at 1B or below, in a 0.7 GB download.

laptop.why: Among the top two open models at 4B and under, in a 1.6 GB download.
Reads pictures natively, and is reported to beat the previous generation's 30B vision models.

workstation.why: The newest open Qwen that reads pictures, at the size a workstation holds.

laptop.why: Scores 94.6 on OmniDocBench at under 1B (the publisher's number), ahead of far larger general models.
Apache-licensed and step-distilled to about 8 GB, and the same download edits pictures too.

workstation.why: The top openly licensed model on Artificial Analysis's open-weights picture board.

laptop.why: Scores 0.92 on LongTextBench, far ahead of other models this size (the ERNIE team's table).

workstation.why: Scores 0.97 on LongTextBench (the publisher's table).

server.why: Ranked first among open models for app and web design on Artificial Analysis (the publisher's report).

laptop.why: Finds what you name in plain words, built into ComfyUI with no add-on.
The standard fill for removing objects: about 0.2 GB, and fast on a CPU.
The best MIT-licensed background remover, built into ComfyUI.
The standard 4x upscaler, in a 0.07 GB download that runs on a CPU.

Apache-licensed, 720p at 24 frames a second, and ComfyUI says it fits an 8 GB graphics card with offloading. A laptop's memory is too tight for it.

A small, permissively licensed speech cleaner that runs in real time on a CPU.
6.3 percent word error in English on the Open ASR Leaderboard, at thousands of times real time.
